insights.headline: Gold's rebound stretches past $4,140 on a softer dollar; rupee near 97 keeps India on edge.
insights.summary: Spot gold extended its rebound from a two-month low to about $4,141 as the dollar eased from an 18-month peak, while silver climbed back above $60. For Indian buyers the relief is partial: the rupee slipped toward 97 per dollar on strong US yields, Brent above $100 and FII outflows, keeping MCX gold near Rs 1.5 lakh per 10 grams, and the RBI's 5.5% repo rate reset adds a domestic rate headwind.
points: Spot gold rose 0.7% to $4,141.09, its second day off a two-month low; silver climbed back above $60.
Traders price an 18% chance of an October Fed hike and 80% for December after split FOMC minutes.
The rupee slid toward 97/dollar on strong US yields, Brent above $100 and persistent FII outflows.
MCX gold held near Rs 1.5 lakh/10g; MCX silver settled 0.51% higher at Rs 2,27,242 per kg.
Analysts expect up to two more RBI hikes this fiscal year after the 25 bps move to 5.5%.

trending.title: The dollar pause is doing gold's heavy lifting
trending.summary: Gold's rebound tracks the dollar's pullback from an 18-month peak almost tick for tick. With markets pricing an 80% December Fed-hike chance, this looks more like relief than a trend change.

trending.title: Rupee near 97: India's gold gets pricier even when it doesn't
trending.summary: A rupee near 97 per dollar raises the landed cost of bullion for Indian buyers, blunting any global dip. Analysts warn of an adverse loop if crude stays above $100.

trending.title: Diwali bid meets Rs 1.5 lakh caution
trending.summary: Jewellery stocks price in a strong festive season - PNGS Reva is up 125% from March - but physical buyers hold back with 24K gold near Rs 1.5 lakh/10g.

trending.title: Silver's round trip: under $60 and back
trending.summary: Silver fell below $60, nearly half of January's record, then recovered with gold. The fundamental debate is live: a widening deficit this year against Deutsche Bank's call for a surplus by 2027.

trending.title: The dip-buyers are still buying
trending.summary: China's biggest monthly reserve add in three years, record Q3 gold-ETF inflows and a survey finding most pros see the pullback as a buying opportunity: the correction is being bought.

items.title: Gold prices recover from two-month low as dollar rally stalls
items.summary: Spot gold rose 0.7% to $4,141.09 on Thursday as the dollar eased from an 18-month peak, extending the rebound from a two-month low hit the previous day. September Fed minutes showed policymakers split on another hike, with traders pricing an 18% chance of an October move and 80% for December; Pepperstone's Chris Weston said gold needs a break above $4,275 to turn constructive.

items.title: INR vs USD: Rupee near 97/dollar; how TCS, Sun Pharma, Tata Steel, SRF may gain from weaker currency
items.summary: The rupee slipped toward the 97-per-dollar mark, pressured by a strong dollar index, elevated US Treasury yields, Brent crude above $100 and persistent FII outflows, Mint reported. Analysts warn a weaker rupee raises landed import costs and imported-inflation risk - a direct headwind for Indian gold buyers, since bullion is priced in dollars.

items.title: Gold near Rs 1.5 lakh/10 grams; silver rises as dollar eases from multi-month high
items.summary: MCX gold held near the Rs 1.5 lakh per 10-gram mark on Thursday as a softer dollar lifted global prices, while MCX silver firmed in line with spot silver's recovery above $60. MCX futures tracked the overnight global move, with silver adding about 0.19% in morning trade.

items.title: RBI's 25 bps Repo Rate Hike: Experts see more! Right time to sell stocks and buy government-backed bonds?
items.summary: After the RBI's 25 bps hike to 5.5% and shift to 'calibrated tightening', Jefferies now sees 75-100 bps of total tightening and some analysts expect up to two more hikes this fiscal year, Mint reported. The piece also quotes strategists advising a shift toward long-term government bonds and, in one view, exiting precious metals for the October-December quarter.

items.title: ET Alpha Wealth Summit 2.0: Equities aren't enough? Praveena Rai makes a case for commodities
items.summary: MCX CEO Praveena Rai told the ET Alpha Wealth Summit that commodities deserve a portfolio slot since they follow different fundamentals than equities, with gold singled out for the safe-haven demand from individuals, institutions and central banks - which she said acquired around 300 tonnes of gold over the last year or two.

items.title: PNGS Reva Diamond Jewellery zooms 35% in two days; up 125% from March low
items.summary: PNGS Reva Diamond Jewellery surged 35% over two sessions to a record Rs 738.40 on heavy volume, up 125% from its March low, after a strong Q2FY27 business update with revenue up 46% excluding gold sales. The company flagged a favorable industry outlook with Dussehra, Diwali and the wedding season ahead.

items.title: Silver Slides Below $60: Why Analysts Still See A Shine Despite 50% Wipeout From Early 2026 Highs
items.summary: Silver slipped below $60 an ounce, nearly 50% under January's record above $120, before recovering back above the level. Analysts cited intact green-energy demand and a widening supply deficit - Metals Focus projects 46.3 million ounces this year - as reasons the metal still has support.

items.title: Deutsche Bank sees silver supply deficit flipping to surplus by 2027
items.summary: Deutsche Bank expects the long-running silver supply deficit to flip into surplus by 2027 as new mine supply and softer industrial offtake catch up with demand. The call sits against the consensus view of a widening deficit this year, making silver's price path unusually contested.

items.title: Strait of Hormuz traffic falls to lowest in over two months after attacks, data shows
items.summary: Commercial traffic through the Strait of Hormuz fell to its lowest in over two months after attacks on Saudi airports killed three people, keeping energy prices elevated and gold's geopolitical safe-haven bid intact. Brent crude held above $100 amid the escalation.

items.title: China posts biggest monthly gold reserve increase in 3 years
items.summary: China added 740,000 ounces to its gold reserves in September, its biggest monthly increase in three years, extending a run of central-bank buying that continues to underpin physical demand even as prices correct. The move keeps official-sector accumulation a key support for the market.

items.title: Gold ETF rush defies 8.5% gold price slide
items.summary: Gold ETFs pulled in a record $31 billion in the third quarter even as bullion prices fell 8.5%, showing investors buying the dip through paper gold. The inflow run contrasts with the spot-price selloff and points to persistent institutional appetite.

items.title: Gold price dips, but buyers remain cautious ahead of Diwali
items.summary: Indian jewellers report buyers are staying cautious ahead of Diwali despite the pullback in gold prices, waiting for further dips before committing to festive purchases. With 24K gold near Rs 1.5 lakh per 10 grams, footfall is being watched more than price charts.

items.title: MCX silver settles 0.51% higher at Rs 2,27,242 as weak US jobs data dims October Fed rate hike hopes
items.summary: MCX silver settled 0.51% higher at Rs 2,27,242 per kg, tracking the global recovery as weak US jobs data cooled expectations of an October Fed hike. The metal held its bounce after slipping below the $60 mark in spot trade.

items.title: MCX gold stays below Rs 1.5 lakh as global prices fall 2 percent; what it means for investors
items.summary: MCX gold traded below Rs 1.5 lakh per 10 grams after global prices fell about 2% on rate-hike bets, and analysts see a negative near-term bias with support near Rs 1,45,000. The piece walks through what the slide means for Indian investors holding through the correction.

items.title: Investors target tokenised gold ETFs after price decrease
items.summary: A survey of 200 professional investors found more than three-quarters view gold's pullback as a buying opportunity, with nearly a quarter of those adding exposure choosing tokenised gold ETFs exclusively. The shift shows digital wrappers gaining ground as a vehicle for bullion exposure.

items.title: Gold, silver price prediction: Will MCX Gold trade with negative bias? check gold price outlook
items.summary: Technical analysts quoted in the piece see MCX gold trading with a negative bias in the near term, eyeing support at Rs 1,45,000 per 10 grams and Rs 2,15,000 per kg for silver. The outlook hinges on the dollar's direction and whether Fed-hike odds keep climbing.
